title: Teacher Kong and His Students
bigQuestion: What makes a good teacher and a good student?

story.title: One Word for a Whole Life
story.kicker: A student asks for one word to live by.
paragraphs: One day a student named Zigong came to his teacher. His teacher was Confucius. Zigong had a big question. He thought about it all day.
He asked, 'Is there one word to guide my whole life?' The other students leaned in. They wanted to hear the answer too. Everyone was quiet.
Confucius thought. Then he gave one word. The word means treating others the way you want to be treated. It was a short word.
Then he explained it. 'Do not do to others what you would not want done to you.' Zigong carried that word with him. He thought about it often.
story.think: If you could keep only one word to guide you, what would it be?

lessons.title: Rich or Poor, Come and Learn
lessons.mainIdea: Confucius taught anyone who wanted to learn, rich or poor.
reading: Long ago, most schools were only for rich families. Confucius did something new. He taught anyone who truly wanted to learn.
The Analects says a student could bring a small gift, like dried meat. Confucius would teach him. Rich or poor did not matter.

words.d: a person who helps others learn

look.title: Open to All
look.text: Anyone who brought even a small gift of dried meat, I never turned away. I taught them all.
look.cite: Analects, book 7, passage 7, retold simply from James Legge's translation (1861)

check.why: Confucius taught anyone who truly wanted to learn.

check.q: What small gift could a student bring?
check.why: Analects 7.7 names a small gift of dried meat.

check.q: Why was this new long ago?
choices: Most schools were for rich families
check.why: Most schools then were only for rich families.

lessons.title: Teachers' Day
lessons.mainIdea: In Taiwan, Teachers' Day is on September 28, the day kept as Confucius's birthday.
reading: In Taiwan, September 28 is Teachers' Day. It is kept as Confucius's birthday. People honor him as a great teacher.
At temples of Confucius, there is a special ceremony with music and dance. Students thank their own teachers too.

words.d: a day to thank teachers; in Taiwan it is September 28
a special event done in a set way to honor someone

look.title: A Picture in Words
look.text: Look at a temple courtyard in the early morning. Musicians play drums and bells. Dancers move slowly, holding long feathers. People stand quietly to honor Confucius.
look.prompt: How are the people showing respect?

check.q: When is Teachers' Day in Taiwan?
check.why: Taiwan keeps Teachers' Day on September 28.

check.q: Whose birthday is kept on that day?
check.why: September 28 is kept as Confucius's birthday.

check.q: What do students do on Teachers' Day?
check.why: Students thank their own teachers on that day.

lessons.title: Yan Hui, Poor and Happy
lessons.mainIdea: Yan Hui was a poor student who stayed happy because he loved to learn.
reading: Yan Hui was Confucius's favorite student. He was very poor. He ate from one small bowl of rice. He lived on a narrow street.
Other people would be sad. But Yan Hui stayed happy. Confucius praised him. He said Yan Hui loved to learn.

words.d: a student of Confucius who was poor but happy

look.title: The Master Praises Yan Hui
look.text: He has one bowl of rice and a gourd of water. He lives on a poor, narrow street. Others could not bear it, but he stays joyful. How good he is!
look.cite: Analects, book 6, passage 9, retold simply from James Legge's translation (1861)
look.prompt: What made Yan Hui happy, even when he had little?

check.why: Yan Hui was poor but stayed happy.

check.q: What did Confucius say Yan Hui loved?
check.why: Confucius said Yan Hui loved to learn.

check.q: How did Confucius feel about Yan Hui?
check.why: Confucius praised Yan Hui in the Analects.

lessons.title: Zilu, Brave and Quick
lessons.mainIdea: Zilu was a brave student who acted fast, and Confucius helped him slow down and think.
reading: Zilu was another student. He was brave and strong. He was quick to act. He always spoke his mind.
Sometimes Zilu acted too fast. Confucius helped him. He taught Zilu to stop and think first. Each student learned in his own way.

words.d: a brave, quick student of Confucius
ready to do hard or scary things

look.title: Two Students, Two Ways
look.text: Yan Hui is quiet. He listens and thinks for a long time. Zilu is loud. He jumps up and acts right away. Confucius gives each one different help.
look.prompt: Why might a teacher give two students different help?

check.why: Zilu was brave and quick to act.

check.q: What did Confucius help Zilu learn?
check.why: Confucius helped Zilu slow down and think first.

check.q: Which student was quiet and poor?
check.why: Yan Hui was the quiet, poor, happy student.

lessons.title: Li: Good Manners
lessons.mainIdea: Confucius taught li, the good manners and customs that show respect.
reading: Confucius cared about manners. The word is li. Li means the right way to act with others. It includes bowing, greeting and sharing.
Confucius taught that manners are more than rules. Good manners show that you care about people.

words.d: good manners and customs that show respect
showing that you think someone matters

look.title: A Picture in Words
look.text: Look at a classroom in the morning. A student bows a little to the teacher. Another holds the door. A third waits for a turn to speak.
look.prompt: Which of these shows li, good manners? Tell why.

check.why: Li means good manners and customs that show respect.

check.q: What do good manners show, as Confucius taught?
choices: That you are in a hurry
check.why: He taught that manners show you care about others.

check.q: Which is an example of li?
check.why: Bowing and greeting are ways of showing respect.

lessons.title: Treat Others Well
lessons.mainIdea: Confucius taught: do not do to others what you would not want done to you.
reading: Remember Zigong's question? He asked for one word to live by. Confucius gave a word that means treating others as you want to be treated.
Then he said: do not do to others what you do not want done to you. It is in the Analects, book 15. Many people remember this teaching.

words.d: treating others the way you want to be treated

look.title: One Word to Live By
look.text: Zigong asked for one word to live by. The Master said: treat others as you would be treated. What you do not want done to you, do not do to others.
look.cite: Analects, book 15, passage 23, retold simply from James Legge's translation (1861)
look.prompt: What does this teaching ask you to think about before you act?

check.q: Who asked Confucius for one word to live by?
check.why: In Analects 15.23, Zigong asks the question.

check.q: What did Confucius teach in his answer?
choices: Do not do to others what you would not want done to you
check.why: His answer asks us to treat others as we want to be treated.

choices: Treating others as you want to be treated
check.why: Reciprocity means treating others the way you want to be treated.

review.why: Confucius taught rich and poor alike.

review.q: Which student was poor but happy?
review.why: Yan Hui was poor and joyful, Analects 6.9 says.

review.q: Which student was brave and quick?
review.why: Zilu was brave and quick to act.
Li means good manners and customs that show respect.

review.q: When is Teachers' Day in Taiwan?
review.why: Taiwan keeps it on September 28, Confucius's birthday.

choices: Do not do to others what you would not want done to you
review.why: That is his answer in Analects 15.23.
